question: What maximum level of vacuum does an MVA syringe typically generate?
explanation: The handheld MVA syringe is specifically engineered to create a strong vacuum ranging between 600 and 660 mmHg when the plunger is locked back. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h1)

question: Why is manual vacuum aspiration generally preferred over sharp metallic curettage in modern practice?

options.A: It relies entirely on high-voltage electrical pumps
options.B: It can only be used in the third trimester of pregnancy
options.C: It has lower complication rates and less blood loss
options.D: It requires general anesthesia in an operating theatre

explanation: MVA is safer, causes less trauma to the myometrium, and results in significantly less bleeding compared to sharp metallic curettage. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h1)

question: What is the maximum gestational age limit safely managed by standard MVA procedures?
explanation: Standard MVA is indicated and safe for uterine evacuations up to the 14th week of gestation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h2)

question: Which condition represents a strict contraindication that must be addressed before performing MVA?

options.A: A closed cervical os in an incomplete miscarriage
options.B: A history of previous lower segment caesarean section

explanation: Instrumenting an infected uterus can drive pathogens upward into the fallopian tubes, worsening pelvic inflammatory disease; infections must be treated first. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the side-openings near the tip of MVA cannulae?

options.A: To allow the injection of local anesthetics
options.B: To measure the exact internal length of the uterine cavity
options.C: To minimize tissue grabbing and reduce perforation risks
options.D: To prevent over-pressurization of the syringe

explanation: The dual side-holes near the tip of Karman cannulae protect the myometrium from aggressive suction trauma and accidental perforation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h3)

question: What component of the MVA syringe maintains the negative pressure before the vacuum is released into the uterus?
explanation: Locking the plunger arms into position at the base of the syringe holds the vacuum state until the clinician opens the valve. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h3)

question: Why is a patient asked to empty her bladder immediately before undergoing an MVA?

options.A: To displace the uterus forward and reduce discomfort
options.B: To prevent urinary tract infections during surgery
options.C: To speed up the absorption of oral antibiotic prophylaxis
options.D: To collect a routine midstream urine sample

explanation: An empty bladder moves out of the surgical path, tilts the uterus into a more favorable position, and lowers procedural pain. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h4)

question: A patient scheduled for MVA expresses severe anxiety and fear of pain. What initial nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Administer immediate intravenous sedatives without further discussion
options.B: Reschedule the procedure for a later date under general anesthesia
options.C: Provide empathetic listening, explain the steps, and discuss pain relief options
options.D: Advise her that discomfort is minimal and requires no intervention

explanation: Clear communication, emotional reassurance, and discussing available pain control measures like a paracervical block effectively reduce procedural anxiety. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h4)

question: What instrument is used to grasp the anterior lip of the cervix and straighten the uterocervical axis?
explanation: The tenaculum provides stable traction on the cervix to straighten the canal for safer passage of instruments. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h5)

question: How does the clinician ensure complete evacuation of the uterine contents once the cannula is inside the cavity?

options.A: By clamping the cervical os tightly with sponge forceps
options.B: By rotating the syringe 180 degrees while moving it gently back and forth
options.C: By pushing the plunger forward repeatedly while the valve remains closed
options.D: By injecting sterile normal saline into the uterine cavity

explanation: Sweeping the cannula tip in a gentle rotational and longitudinal motion ensures all walls of the cavity are cleared of tissue. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h5)

question: What is the primary reason for inspecting the evacuated tissue in a strainer after an MVA?

options.A: To confirm complete evacuation and verify products of conception
options.B: To separate blood clots from viable embryonic stem cells
options.C: To sterilize the tissue samples for laboratory pathology
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the products of conception

explanation: Inspecting tissue ensures that all gestational tissue has been removed and rules out molar pregnancy or ectopic tissue. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h6)

question: Which nursing intervention is essential during the immediate recovery phase following an MVA?

options.A: Applying hot water bottles directly to the abdomen
options.B: Encouraging immediate ambulation around the ward
options.C: Monitoring vital signs and vaginal bleeding every 15 minutes
options.D: Administering strong general anesthetics for post-op pain

explanation: Close observation during the first hour helps catch hemorrhage or shock early when interventions are most effective. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h6)

question: What is the classic clinical sign that suggests a uterine perforation has occurred during instrumentation?

options.A: Sudden and severe swelling of the external genitalia
options.B: Instruments passing deeper than expected without normal resistance
options.C: An immediate drop in body temperature
options.D: A complete absence of any vaginal bleeding

explanation: When a sound or cannula slips past the normal uterine depth without encountering muscular resistance, perforation of the uterine wall must be suspected. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h7)

question: A patient returns to the clinic five days post-MVA with lower abdominal pain, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, and fever. What complication is most likely?
explanation: Fever, foul discharge, and pelvic pain days after a uterine evacuation strongly point toward an ascending pelvic or endometrial infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h7)

question: What is the first step in processing MVA instruments immediately after a procedure is completed?

options.C: Scrubbing with abrasive steel wool brushes
options.D: Lubrication of all O-rings with silicone oil

explanation: Decontaminating instruments in chlorine solution inactivates infectious pathogens before staff handle them for cleaning. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h8)

question: Why is medical-grade silicone oil applied to the O-rings of an MVA syringe during reprocessing?

options.A: To prevent rust formation on metallic components
options.B: To disinfect the inner chamber against bacterial spores
options.C: To accelerate the drying process after high-level disinfection
options.D: To maintain an airtight vacuum seal within the cylinder

explanation: Silicone oil lubricates the plunger and O-ring, ensuring smooth movement and a tight seal necessary to hold negative pressure. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h8)
